purpose: Visual design exploration; no application code changes. Mockup text and shortcuts are illustrative.

concepts.name: Obsidian
concepts.prompt: Use case: ui-mockup. Generate one high fidelity desktop browser concept for Arbiter, direction 1 "Obsidian". This is a design exploration for an existing distraction-free Qt desktop browser whose websites fill the window: no persistent toolbar, address bar, tab strip or sidebar, hidden titlebar and window buttons. Deliver a wide landscape polished flat app screenshot, straight on, large enough for UI details, no laptop hardware or perspective mockup. Show a rounded 1280x820 browser window on a quiet neutral backdrop occupying almost the whole image. Background website is a tasteful readable design journal article with monochrome photography of concrete architecture, very subtly dimmed. Main subject is the Arbiter command/address overlay in the upper middle: a restrained 640px-wide charcoal panel, crisp one pixel neutral border, 14px radius, extremely subtle shadow, clear white SF-style typography, large address/search input reading "Search or enter address", understated search glyph and Cmd L hint, divider, 3 recently visited rows with small simple favicon marks, titles "Linear", "GitHub", "Design notes", muted full domains, keyboard selection highlight and Return key hint. Small footer actions "Tabs" and "Passwords" with keyboard hints. Generous but purposeful spacing, precise alignment, no huge padding. A small secondary inset lower right shows the matching native passkey sheet titled "Sign in to github.com" with actions "Use Arbiter passkey" and "Use a phone". Primary aesthetic near-black graphite with sophisticated gray tonal separation, honest legible UI, subtly tactile without shiny effects. Tiny caption outside window "01 / Obsidian". No colorful gradients, no AI sparkle icons, no dashboards, no permanent chrome, no big branding on the website. This is a concept illustration, not a claim of existing functionality.

concepts.name: Paper
concepts.prompt: Use case: ui-mockup. Generate one high fidelity desktop browser concept for Arbiter, direction 2 "Paper". A warm editorial reinterpretation of an existing distraction-free Qt browser. Websites occupy the entire rounded window with no persistent toolbar, tab strip, address bar or sidebar and hidden window buttons. Deliver a wide landscape flat screenshot-style design presentation, straight on, no laptop hardware, no perspective, no 3D. Main window 1280x820 almost fills frame, on quiet warm neutral background. Show Arbiter's on-demand tab overview taking most of the window: warm ivory surface, dark ink typography, very restrained desaturated clay accent only for selected state, fine warm-gray rules, subtle 12px corner radii, no heavy shadows. Top left small word "Tabs", right small "Esc" keycap. Below a beautifully proportioned search input reading "Find a tab". Six large page-preview cards arranged 3 columns by 2 rows, with convincing website thumbnail previews, clear page titles and muted domains below. Titles "Design notes", "Arbiter", "Reading list", "GitHub", "Linear", "Architecture". The selected card has a fine clay outline and a tiny active indicator, inactive cards quieter. Bottom compact subtle action "New tab" plus Cmd T hint. Natural typographic hierarchy, generous whitespace, elegant typography combining a quiet editorial serif only for the overview heading and clean sans serif for controls. A small inset at lower right overlapping only a little edge shows the matching warm address popup: text "Search or enter address", two recent rows. Tiny caption outside window "02 / Paper". Keep the emphasis on browser interface rather than website design, warm and calm but efficient, no widgets, no bookmarks dashboard, no imaginary workspaces or AI features. This is a proposed visual concept.

concepts.name: Glacier
concepts.prompt: Use case: ui-mockup. Generate one high fidelity desktop browser concept for Arbiter, direction 3 "Glacier". A native-feeling translucent desktop browser that retains immersive full-window websites. No persistent toolbar, address bar, tab strip or sidebar; navigation controls appear only on demand. Deliver one wide landscape flat screenshot-style UI concept, straight-on, no laptop hardware, no perspective. Rounded 1280x820 app window almost fills the frame against a subtle cool gray background. Background website is a refined travel photography journal with a large mountain lake photograph and understated article typography, full bleed to app edges; don't redesign a dashboard. Show a floating address/search panel in upper middle with believable macOS-style frosted material, soft milky translucency, finely defined edge and restrained blue selected-row accent. Legibility is paramount: strong dark charcoal type on light frosted panel, calm hierarchy, no excessive blur. Search input reads "Search or enter address", below a compact list with "GitHub", "Design notes", "Reading list" and muted domains. At bottom center show a small revealed navigation capsule hovering over page, containing back, forward, reload, current domain "fieldnotes.example", tabs count "6", and simple more icon. This is explicitly an on-demand reveal state, not a permanent toolbar. A discreet instruction below the window reads "Controls when you need them." A small secondary inset lower right shows a matching compact credential popover titled "Sign in" with "Arbiter passkey" and "Use a phone" actions, positioned clear of the capsule. Beautifully controlled glass depth, understated cool whites, pale slate and single icy blue accent. Avoid rainbow glass, thick glossy bevels, giant rounded pills, AI sparkle icons, busy chrome or sidebars. Tiny caption outside window "03 / Glacier". This is a proposed design exploration.

glacier_correction_prompt: Edit this UI concept with a minimal text-only correction. Preserve the entire Glacier browser mockup, composition, mountain website, glass panels, colors, type scale, layout and labels exactly. In the lower-right sign-in card replace the subtitle below "Arbiter passkey", currently "Sign in with Face ID", with the exact text "Verify vault passphrase". Replace the subtitle under "Use a phone", currently "Get a one-time code", with the exact text "Scan a QR code". No other changes. This browser has passphrase verification and a phone QR flow, not Face ID or OTP.
